items.title: Fix KillSwitch.clear() to reset self._tripped
items.why_now: Critical confirmed bug: clear() deletes marker files but leaves self._tripped=True, causing subsequent reads to indicate switch still tripped. This breaks the kill switch contract and can halt the loop after a clear.

steps.do: Add self._tripped = False at the end of clear() method
steps.verified_by: Run grep -A 10 'def clear' daedalus/spine/killswitch.py and confirm self._tripped = False is present. Also run existing tests for KillSwitch to ensure no regression.

items.assumption: The clear() method is defined in daedalus/spine/killswitch.py; we assume its structure allows a one-line fix. The settling check grep will verify.

items.title: Verify session attribute initialization in Session class
items.why_now: High severity: if Session objects lack timeout_s, started_at, or cwd, subprocess_adapter.py will AttributeError. This blocks the vertical slice if sessions are used.

steps.do: Run grep -rn 'class Session' daedalus/ to find session definition and check if attributes have defaults.
steps.verified_by: Observe output; if definition found, inspect for dataclass defaults or __init__ that sets these attributes.

steps.do: If no defaults found, trace creation paths in subprocess_adapter.py and picker.py to see if attributes are guaranteed before access.

items.assumption: Session class definition exists somewhere under daedalous/. The settling check grep will locate it.

items.title: Check if any consumer uses search() wrapper instead of search_report
items.why_now: High severity: if picker or other module uses search() (compatibility shim), it loses freshness info and may use stale embeddings. This affects correctness of the picker.

steps.do: Search for calls to 'search(' in the picker and other modules; if any call the compatibility wrapper, verify they also check freshness via other means.
steps.verified_by: grep -rn 'search(' daedalous/ -- exclude test files. Examine each call site.

items.assumption: The picker module and other relevant files are under daedalous/. The settling check grep will find them.

items.title: Check if any consumer distinguishes empty vs missing DAEDALUS_TRACE_ID
items.why_now: Low severity: if prior_env is empty string, restoration sets empty string instead of deleting key. Only matters if consumer treats empty differently from missing.

steps.do: Search for all consumers of DAEDALUS_TRACE_ID and check if any treat empty string differently from missing.
steps.verified_by: grep -rn 'DAEDALUS_TRACE_ID' daedalous/ and inspect each usage for os.environ.get vs 'in os.environ' pattern.

items.assumption: DAEDALUS_TRACE_ID is used somewhere in the codebase; the grep will find all occurrences.
